summary: Typosquat postinstall exfiltrates host identity to webhook.site collector
details: Package name resembles the Twilio brand but the code contains no Twilio functionality. The package.json postinstall hook executes index.js at npm install, which collects os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username, process.cwd(), and npm_package_name and POSTs them as JSON to a hardcoded webhook.site endpoint (https://webhook.site/42ce0f0e-a0a0-41b5-b157-1c0f918e064f). The behavior is a host-identity beacon consistent with dependency-confusion / typosquat reconnaissance: installing the package causes the installer's machine identifiers to leave to an attacker-controlled collector with no functionality benefit to the caller. Version 99.99.99 is the canonical dependency-confusion overshoot version.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
